verses.zh: 耶户第七年，约阿施登基，在耶路撒冷作王四十年。他母亲名叫西比亚，是别是巴人。
verses.en: (12:2) In Jehu’s seventh year Jehoash became king; he reigned for 40 years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother was Zibiah, who was from Beer Sheba.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
12:1 "he reigned forty years" There are two ways to view this number.

- It is a round number ‒ see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7.

- It counts the reign of Athaliah, thereby counting from Ahaziah ‒ see

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED MONARCHY.

▣ "his mother's name was Zibiah" Jehoash was not a son of Athaliah.

▣ "Jehoash did right in the sight of the Lord" This was true as long as
Jehoiada was his counselor. This is a recurrent idiom related to a godly king (cf. Deut. 6:18; 12:28; 13:18; 1 Kgs. 11:38;
14:8; 15:11; 22:43; 2 Chr. 14:2; 20:32; 24:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "the priest" This was a way to designate the head priest. In v. 16 the ADJECTIVE
"great" (BDB 152) designates the same person. It is usually translated "High Priest." See a good brief note on the
changing titles for the High Priest in Roland deVauz, Ancient Israel, pp. 377-379.

verses.zh: 约阿施在祭司耶何耶大教训他的时候，就行耶和华眼中看为正的事；
verses.en: Jehoash did what the Lord approved[NOTE:1] all his days when[NOTE:2] Jehoiada the priest taught him.
notes: Heb “what was proper in the eyes of the Lord.”

The MT reads יָמָיו אֲשֶׁר (yamayv ʾasher, “all his days which…”). The LXX says “all the days which Jehoiada the priest enlightened him,” implying either יָמִים (yamim, “days”) or יְמֵי (yeme, “days of”), without the pronominal suffix. Lev 13:46 demonstrates that יְמֵי can be in construct with an אֲשֶׁר clause, but an אֲשֶׁר clause can also follow יוֹם (yom “day”) when it has a pronominal suffix. In either case the אֲשֶׁר clause restricts the time period that יוֹם describes. Therefore this verse does not contradict 2 Chr 24:2 which limits its praise of the king to “all the days of Jehoiada the priest.”

verses.zh: 只是邱坛还没有废去，百姓仍在那里献祭烧香。
verses.en: But the high places were not eliminated; the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense on the high places.
verses.commentary:
12:3 "the high places" These were local places of worship (BDB 119). Originally they were not condemned
but with the rise of a mandated central shrine in Jerusalem, they became identified with Ba'al worship.

Not until Hezekiah (2 Kgs. 18:4) were the high places destroyed (cf. 1 Kgs. 15:14; 22:43;
2 Kgs. 12:3; 14:4; 15:4,35).

verses.zh: 约阿施对众祭司说：「凡奉到耶和华殿分别为圣之物所值通用的银子，或各人当纳的身价，或乐意奉到耶和华殿的银子，
verses.en: Jehoash said to the priests, “I place at your disposal[NOTE:1] all the consecrated silver that has been brought to the Lord’s temple, including the silver collected from the census tax,[NOTE:2] the silver received from those who have made vows,[NOTE:3] and all the silver that people have voluntarily contributed to the Lord’s temple.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “I place at your disposal” are added in the translation for clarification.

Heb “the silver of passing over a man.” The precise meaning of the phrase is debated, but עָבַר (ʿavar), “pass over,” probably refers here to counting, suggesting the reference is to a census conducted for taxation purposes. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 137.

Heb “the silver of persons, his valuation.” The precise meaning of the phrase is uncertain, but parallels in Lev 27 suggest that personal vows are referred to here. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 137.
Heb “all the silver which goes up on the heart of a man to bring to the house of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
12:4-5 The temple of Solomon had been neglected, especially under Athaliah. It needed to be repaired.
King Jehoash started the campaign to do this by collecting some of the revenue of the temple.

- each man's assessment ‒ Exod. 30:11-16; Num. 18:19; 2 Chr. 24:9, for priests (AB, p. 137 and NET Bible call it
"a census tax")

- free will offerings ‒ for any purpose (like peace offerings)

- vow offerings ‒ Lev. 27:1-13

verses.zh: 你们当从所认识的人收了来，修理殿的一切破坏之处。」
verses.en: The priests should receive the silver they need from the treasurers and repair any damage to the temple they discover.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Let the priests take for themselves, each from his treasurer, and let them repair the damage of the temple, with respect to all the damage that is found there.” The word מַכָּר (makar), translated here “treasurer,” occurs only in this passage. Some suggest it means “merchant” or “benefactor.” Its usage in Ugaritic texts, where it appears in a list of temple officials, suggests that it refers in this context to individuals who were in charge of disbursing temple funds.

verses.zh: 无奈到了约阿施王二十三年，祭司仍未修理殿的破坏之处。
verses.en: By the twenty-third year of King Jehoash’s reign the priests had still not repaired the damage to the temple.
verses.commentary:
12:6-15 For some reason not given, the priests did not use the money for repairs (cf. 2 Chr. 24:5).
Because of this, King Jehoash demanded the collected money

- be used exclusively for temple repair (v. 7)

- be kept by both a royal representative and a priestly representative (v. 11)

- be given directly to the laborers and craftsmen (v. 12)

- there would be no required accounting from the workmen of the disbursement of the funds (v. 15, this may
be a slap at the priests' handling of the money)

The NET Bible, p. 611, #21, suggests this reluctance on the part of the priests to repair the temple
was due to the fact they wanted skilled workers to repair it, not themselves.

verses.zh: 所以约阿施王召了大祭司耶何耶大和众祭司来，对他们说：「你们怎么不修理殿的破坏之处呢？从今以后，你们不要从所认识的人再收银子，要将所收的交出来，修理殿的破坏之处。」
verses.en: So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest along with the other priests, and said to them, “Why have you not repaired the damage to the temple? Now, take no more silver from your treasurers unless you intend to use it to repair the damage.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Now, do not take silver from your treasurers because for the damages to the temple you must give it.”

verses.zh: 众祭司答应不再收百姓的银子，也不修理殿的破坏之处。
verses.en: The priests agreed[NOTE:1] not to collect silver from the people and relieved themselves of personal responsibility for the temple repairs.[NOTE:2]
notes: Outside of this passage the verb אוּת (ʾut) appears only in Gen 34:15-22.

Heb “and not to repair the damages to the temple.” This does not mean that the priests were no longer interested in repairing the temple. As the following context makes clear, the priests decided to hire skilled workers to repair the damage to the temple, rather than trying to make the repairs themselves.

verses.zh: 祭司耶何耶大取了一个柜子，在柜盖上钻了一个窟窿，放于坛旁，在进耶和华殿的右边；守门的祭司将奉到耶和华殿的一切银子投在柜里。
verses.en: Jehoiada the priest took a chest and drilled a hole in its lid. He placed it on the right side of the altar near the entrance of[NOTE:1] the Lord’s temple. The priests who guarded the entrance would put into it all the silver brought to the Lord’s temple.
notes: Heb “on the right of the altar as a man enters.”

verses.zh: 他们见柜里的银子多了，便叫王的书记和大祭司上来，将耶和华殿里的银子数算包起来。
verses.en: When they saw the chest was full of silver, the royal secretary[NOTE:1] and the high priest counted the silver that had been brought to the Lord’s temple and bagged it up.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the king’s scribe.”

Heb “went up and tied [it] and counted the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.” The order of the clauses has been rearranged in the translation to make better sense in English, since it seems more logical to count the money before bagging it (cf. NIV, NCV, NRSV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
12:10 "the king's scribe" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SCRIBES.

▣

NASB, NRSV, Peshitta (צור)

"tied"

NKJV, NJB, JPSOA
"put it"

TEV, REB (צרר)

"melt down"

LXX
"bundled"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 848 II, KB 1015, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw), which means "to confine," "to bind," and "to besiege." The UBS Text Project, p. 356, gives the MT a "B"
rating (some doubt).

The NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 792, asserts that both roots refer to a melting process related to valuable metals.
There were no coins in the ANE in this period. Gifts would be in the form of

- pieces of metal

- pieces of jewelry

verses.zh: 把所平的银子交给督工的，就是耶和华殿里办事的人；他们把银子转交修理耶和华殿的木匠和工人，
verses.en: They would then hand over[NOTE:1] the silver that had been weighed to the construction foremen[NOTE:2] assigned to the Lord’s temple. They hired carpenters and builders to work on the Lord’s temple,
notes: Heb “would give.”
Heb “doers of the work.”
verses.commentary:
12:11-12 Notice the type of laborers that were hired.

- the carpenters ‒ BDB 781 (lit. "craftsmen in wood," NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 298-299)

- the builders ‒ BDB 124, KB 139, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- the masons ‒ BDB 154, KB 180, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- the stonecutters

- stone ‒ BDB 6

- cutters ‒ BDB 345, KB 342, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- those who brought (BDB 888, KB 1111, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) the materials

- timber ‒ BDB 781 (see #1)

- hewn stone ‒ BDB 6 CONSTRUCT BDB 345

verses.zh: 并瓦匠、石匠，又买木料和凿成的石头，修理耶和华殿的破坏之处，以及修理殿的各样使用。
verses.en: as well as masons and stonecutters. They bought wood and chiseled stone to repair the damage to the Lord’s temple and also paid for all the other expenses.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and for all that which was going out concerning the house for repair.”

verses.zh: 但那奉到耶和华殿的银子，没有用以做耶和华殿里的银杯、蜡剪、碗、号，和别样的金银器皿，
verses.en: The silver brought to the Lord’s temple was not used for silver bowls, trimming shears, basins, trumpets, or any kind of gold or silver implements.
verses.commentary:
12:13 The text in 2 Kings wants all the money collected to go to the repairs of the building. 2 Chronicles 24:14 tells
us there was some money left over and this was used for temple utensils.

verses.zh: 乃将那银子交给督工的人修理耶和华的殿；
verses.en: It was handed over[NOTE:1] to the foremen who used it to repair the Lord’s temple.
notes: Heb “was given.”

verses.zh: 且将银子交给办事的人转交做工的人，不与他们算账，因为他们办事诚实。
verses.en: They did not audit the treasurers who disbursed[NOTE:1] the funds to the foremen, for they were honest.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “gave.”
Heb “and they did not conduct a reckoning of the men who gave the silver into their hand to give to the doers of the work, for in honesty they were working.”
verses.commentary:
12:15 "faithfully" This is one of the great Hebrew roots/words. In the OT its main thrust is "faithfulness."
In this context it may be a contrast to the priests who initially wasted the money collected for repairing the temple
of Solomon.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH, AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OLD TESTAMENT

verses.zh: 惟有赎愆祭、赎罪祭的银子没有奉到耶和华的殿，都归祭司。
verses.en: (The silver collected in conjunction with reparation offerings and sin offerings was not brought to the Lord’s temple; it belonged to the priests.)
verses.commentary:
12:16 The priests did retain their personal income from

- guilt offerings ‒ see Lev. 5:14-6:7; 7:1-2; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 557-565

- sin offerings ‒ see Lev. 4:1-5:13; 6:24-30

verses.zh: 那时，亚兰王哈薛上来攻打迦特，攻取了，就定意上来攻打耶路撒冷。
verses.en: At that time King Hazael of Syria attacked[NOTE:1] Gath and captured it. Hazael then decided to attack Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “went up and fought against.”
Heb “Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.”
verses.commentary:
12:17-18 Hazael continues his invasions. He controlled the trans-Jordan area but wanted more (see more
details in 2 Chr. 24:23-27).

It is ironic that the priests were reluctant to use their income for temple repair; all the treasures
of the temple and palace are used to pay off the Syrians.

verses.zh: 犹大王约阿施将他列祖犹大王约沙法、约兰、亚哈谢所分别为圣的物和自己所分别为圣的物，并耶和华殿与王宫府库里所有的金子都送给亚兰王哈薛；哈薛就不上耶路撒冷来了。
verses.en: King Jehoash of Judah collected all the sacred items that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, had consecrated, as well as his own sacred items and all the gold that could be found in the treasuries of the Lord’s temple and the royal palace. He sent it all[NOTE:1] to King Hazael of Syria, who then withdrew[NOTE:2] from Jerusalem.
notes: The object (“it all”) is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “went up.”

verses.zh: 约阿施其余的事，凡他所行的都写在犹大列王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Joash’s reign, including all his accomplishments, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Joash, and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”
verses.commentary:
12:19-21 The text does not state why Jehoash was assassinated by his own servants, but since these men
did not flee, one is caused to assume that

- Jehoash had done something, possibly idolatry (cf. 2 Chr. 24:15-22)

- the king's actions were well known and not approved by the people

- his death was not a coup but a judgment (later these men were killed, cf. 2 Kgs. 14:5)

- these men were sons of foreign women; why it affected their actions is uncertain

verses.zh: 约阿施的臣仆起来背叛，在下悉拉的米罗宫那里将他杀了。
verses.en: His servants conspired against him[NOTE:1] and murdered Joash at Beth Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “rose up and conspired [with] a conspiracy.”
Heb “Beth Millo which goes down [toward] Silla.”
verses.commentary:
12:20 "conspiracy" The VERB basically means "to bind." Here, to bind together for a conspiracy.
Both the NOUN and the VERB appear together (BDB 905, KB 1153).

▣ "the house of Millo" See notes on "millo" (BDB 571) at 2 Sam. 5:9 and 1 Kgs. 11:27.

▣ "to Silla" This city/village/place (BDB 698) occurs only here and is unknown. It is omitted in the LXX.

verses.zh: 杀他的那臣仆就是示米押的儿子约撒甲和朔默的儿子约萨拔。众人将他葬在大卫城他列祖的坟地里。他儿子亚玛谢接续他作王。
verses.en: His servants Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer murdered him.[NOTE:1] He was buried[NOTE:2] with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Amaziah replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “struck him down and he died.”
Heb “they buried him.”
verses.commentary:
12:21

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA
"Jozacar"

NKJV, REB, Peshitta
"Jozachar"

LXX
"Iezichar"

NET Bible
"Jozabad"

This person is called "Zabad" in 2 Chr. 24:26. The UBS Text Project, p. 356, could not decide
between "Jozacar" or "Jozachar," but gave them both "D" ratings (highly doubtful).

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What does it mean "to do right in the sight of the Lord"?

- What were the high places?

- Why had the priests "not repaired the damages of the house" (v. 6)?

- What was Jehoash's new procedure about the temple upkeep?

- Define "the sacred things" (v. 18).
